newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lafarge sees stable 96 operating profit.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge sees stable 96 operating profit.

text.p: French building materials company Lafarge expects an improved second half compared to the first six months and aims to post operating profits similar to 1995, chairman Bertrand Collomb said on Wednesday.

"The second half should...be better than the first and our objective is to reach an annual operating profit, excluding exceptionals, similar to that of last year," he said in a statement with first-half results.
"We see encouraging signs of recovery in some of our markets," he said.
Lafarge posted full-year 1995 operating profit, excluding exceptionals, of 4.04 billion francs.
The group reported a 53 percent drop in 1996 first-half net attributable profit to 545 million francs from 1.15 billion a year ago.
Collomb said the first quarter of 1996 had been "particularly difficult," with an extremely severe winter which led to a loss in volumes.

The second quarter was a period of contrasts -- weakness in France, where the construction industry saw the most difficult conditions for a long time, a mediocre western European market, strength in the United States and excellent conditions in some emerging markets.
Collomb said it was the unusual coincidence of these factors and the absence of exceptional elements which lay behind the fall in first-half results.

Lafarge will pursue its expansion strategy, which would allow it eventually to benefit from the dynamism of certain markets. It will invest between seven and eight billion francs this year, he said. It invested two billion francs in the first half.
